assertion_analysis.failure_condition: assert composed[SHIM_PYTHON_ENV] == sys.executable fails if _persisted_worker_environment stops writing RECKON_SHIM_PYTHON; the right-hand side is the interpreter running the test, independent of anything the test hands the code, and the declared negative control reddens it with KeyError('RECKON_SHIM_PYTHON') in negative-control.log.

assert kept[SHIM_PYTHON_ENV] == chosen fails if the composer overwrites a value the caller already supplied; chosen is the value passed in, but the guarded defect (an unconditional assignment to sys.executable) is exactly an overwrite of the pass-through, so the assertion reddens on the regression even though both sides name the same literal.

assert STUB_MARKER not in result.stderr fails if the shim resolves the stub python3.12 rather than the composing interpreter; the marker is emitted only by the planted stub, an independent artefact of the run, and negative-control.log shows it reddening with 'STUB-PYTHON3.12-RAN'.

assert result.returncode == 0 and 'TOOL=srun' in result.stdout fail if the shim dies before reaching its main or forwards nothing; TOOL=srun is printed by the planted fake srun, independent of the composed environment.

the widened set-equality assertions fail if _persisted_worker_environment stops adding RECKON_SHIM_PYTHON, since each compares the produced key set to a literal set naming it; both sides are not the same value, and the base arm without the production change (44 passed, 7 files) shows the file is exercised.
